title: legal redlines scratchpad - enterprise contract notes
content:
Purpose:
Quick personal scratchpad for clauses we should flag during enterprise contract redlines. Mostly talking points for commercial/legal when negotiating Dedicated/Private deals (customers asking for SKUs, KMS, audit logs, and expanded SLAs).

High-priority clauses to watch:
1) Data processing & customer data ownership
- Watch for language that claims 'customer grants rights to use' vs. standard processing-for-delivery wording. Push to keep 'processing only to provide the service' + explicit prohibition on model training unless we agree.
- If customer requests export/backups, confirm scope: snapshots of models vs. inference logs. For Private deployments accept export of customer-owned configs and logs, but not proprietary runtime code or our optimization configs.

2) Security / KMS / key custody
- Customers often want HSM/KMS control (bring-your-own-key). Acceptable for Private (on-prem/VPC) with documented operational responsibilities. For Hosted API we do BYOK with envelope encryption, but we must limit scope of access and require attestation.
- Talking point: we can offer KMS integration but will need limited support windows and additional SOW for key rotations and incident response.

3) SLA, outage credits & remedies
- Standard position: uptime SLA for Dedicated (tiered) with service credits only, no termination for SLA failures except repeated/unmitigated breaches. Avoid immediate termination for single incidents.
- Push back on excessive caps or unlimited credits; propose cap = monthly recurring charges up to X%. Use examples: 99.9% for Dedicated (SLA credit ladder). For Private deployments, SLA is limited to control plane only; call out customer infrastructure dependencies.

4) Indemnities & liability caps
- Keep aggregate liability cap at fees paid in prior 12 months (standard). Customer tries to move to higher cap for PII/data breaches — negotiate carve-outs: cannot exceed cap except for gross negligence or willful misconduct and IP infringement (we may accept higher cap for IP in some cases).

5) Data breach notification & cooperation
- Ensure timeline for notifications (48-72 hrs for suspected breaches) and define roles (we notify if our systems compromised; customer notifies if their credentials compromised).
- For Private/on-prem deployments, we are not responsible for customer-managed infra; limit obligations to our control plane and software patches where applicable.

6) Audit rights & compliance
- Customer asks for deep audits/pen tests. Offer SOC2 reports and limited penetration tests with pre-approved scope and scheduled windows. Deny unlimited on-prem audits.
- For regulated customers, suggest remote/replicated evidence and redacted logs rather than full access to our internal dashboards.

7) IP & model outputs
- Clarify that customer owns content they input and model outputs generated for them. Avoid language that assigns model improvements or derivative rights to customer. Conversely, we should not be construed as owning customer prompts.

8) Termination & transition assistance
- Standard: 30-90 days for transition assistance; chargeable beyond a baseline. For high-value customers consider 6 months migration support with fees. Preserve right to retain anonymized operational metrics.

Negotiation playbook / suggested language:
- For training prohibition: 'Provider will not use Customer Data to improve or train Provider's models without Customer's explicit written consent.'
- For KMS: 'Customer may provide KMS keys under BYOK; Provider will implement envelope encryption and will not export plaintext key material. Support for BYOK will be delivered under separate SOW where operational runbooks and rotation responsibilities are documented.'
- For SLA credits: insert a three-tier ladder (99.9%+, 99.5%-99.9%, <99.5%) with incremental credit percentages and monthly cap at 50% of monthly fee. Termination only after 3 consecutive months below X threshold and failure to remediate.

Open questions / redlines to add next pass:
- Customer requested clause letting them run our runtime in their cloud with custom patches — need engineering input: acceptable? If allowed, must be under a paid license, no access to core optimization kernels, and strict code escrow.
- Data residency vs. caching: customers want guaranteed KV cache eviction on demand. Need to confirm technical feasibility and propose SLA for cache wipe.
- Export of logs for e-discovery: propose redacted logs with PII removal; full logs only under legal process.

References to use when pushing back:
- Link to SOC2 summary + addendum (attach to proposal).
- Example clause from Enterprise Contract Playbook (Confluence link above).

Quick negotiator talking points (one-liners):
- 'We can support BYOK in Private deployments, but it requires a follow-up SOW for ongoing key ops.'
- 'SLA credits are the primary remedy; termination for a single outage is disproportionate — propose escalation & remediation first.'
- 'We do not train models on customer data without written consent — protects both parties.'
- 'For on-prem/Private, responsibilities are shared; we can't guarantee uptime of customer-managed infra.'

Action items (to self):
- Draft redline snippets for KMS, SLA ladder, training prohibition by 2026-01-25.
- Sync with Eng (Nina Patel) on cache-eviction feasibility and timeline.
- Pull latest SOC2 report and update linked artifacts in Confluence.

Notes to self: keep the doc lean — this is a living scratchpad. Save final language to Confluence once agreed.

End of scratchpad.
